words.gloss: one who does not harbor or cherish

literal: One of great generosity, who does not cherish anger, than him, those who have surrounding relations, on this great earth, there is none.
translation: There is no one on this vast earth who possesses more surrounding kinsmen than a person of great generosity who does not harbor anger.
modern: பெரிய கொடையாளனாகவும், கோபத்தைக் கொள்ளாதவனாகவும் இருப்பவனை விட, அதிகமான சுற்றத்தாரைப் பெற்றவர் இந்த பெரிய உலகத்தில் யாரும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights the two essential qualities required to attract and retain a large circle of relatives and friends: boundless generosity and freedom from anger. A person who gives freely to those in need and never harbors resentment or anger will naturally draw people toward them. The poet asserts that such an individual will have the largest network of supportive relations on earth. The word 'maruṅku' refers to one's side or surrounding relations, emphasizing how these virtues keep people closely bound to one's side.
